newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate seen down.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's bellwether one-month Cetes rate seen down.

text.p: Renewed stability in the Mexican peso will help rates on Mexican Cetes, or treasury bills, to fall slightly at the primary auction on Tuesday, analysts said on Monday.
"The exchange rate is helping ease pressure on rates. Although the volume has not been great, there have been longer-term trades lower than the average rate," said one analyst.
After weakening through 8.0 pesos per dollar recently, the peso closed on Monday at about 7.9 per dollar.
The recovery of the peso has helped ease rates in the secondary money market as well.
The rate on the bellwether 28-day Cetes rose to 29.34 percent last week, the fourth increase in a row. It was as low as 22.74 percent in early October.

"The attention of investors and market players has been centered in the medium and long terms (six-month and one-year), which shows that there is some confidence from them in the recovery of the economy," said a report from Grupo Financiero Inverlat.
The high real rates Cetes are paying are paying will allow nominal Cetes rates to fall, analysts said.

"Whereas real rate in pesos will naturally tend to decline due to the higher inflation in November and especially in December, the expected return in dollars is very attractive," said the brokerage house Interacciones in an analysis.

While the majority of analysts expect the rate on 28-day paper to fall, analysts are not ruling out that one-month paper will come under pressure before the government defines its budget criteria for 1997 this week.
"The next meeting of the (U.S.) Federal Reserve and the announcement of the government's economic criteria are also influencing interest rates," said one analyst.
The Finance Minister will outline the government's economic picture for 1997 before the Congress on November 7.
The central bank will offer 3.3 billion pesos worth Cetes this week.
